m6_holdout_global_prior_finding_2026-09-: While verifying (not assuming) WHY the multihop witness's evidence improved holdout Brier, discovered a much broader structural fact affecting every M6/M7 calibration number this project has ever reported, including the original already-VALIDATED M6 v0.2 baseline (holdout Brier=0.48125, closed 2026-09-17): StructuralLearningPolicy.predict() has NEVER used BASIS_EXACT_BUCKET or BASIS_RULE_ONLY on any holdout evaluation -- 100% of holdout predictions fall back to BASIS_GLOBAL_PRIOR. Root cause, structural and by design (not a bug): split_by_rule() guarantees a rule never appears in both train and holdout, so a holdout record's rule signature is never present in the trained policy's bucket/rule counts. Consequence: every Brier/ECE number this project has reported measures whether the GLOBAL training class-frequency prior generalizes to new rules -- never rule-specific learning, despite the module's name and stated goal (Rule x Context x Depth x Provenance -> distribution). This does NOT invalidate the third-party validations (which always explicitly scoped their claims to mechanism honesty/reproducibility, never to rule-specific generalization -- see each protocol's 'Scientific non-closure' section) but corrects the informal reading of these Brier numbers as demonstrating structural learning. The initial hypothesis offered for the multihop witness's improvement ('same bias reproduces identically in train and holdout of the same rule') was checked directly and found to be STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE (confirmed false, not just superseded) -- the real, verified mechanism is a shift in the GLOBAL prior only. Verified robust-ness across 10 random splits: the multihop addition improves Brier in 8/10 seeds and WORSENS it in 2/10 -- not a guaranteed, causal improvement, a statistical tendency tied to how well the shifted prior happens to match a given holdout's composition. 3 new permanent tests (tests/test_m6_holdout_basis_diagnosis_v0_1.py) document this as CURRENT state (not enforced as a permanent invariant, since a future richer corpus reaching rule-specific holdout evaluation would be a genuine improvement, not a regression). 441/441 tests passing, zero regression.
